<description>
The current documentation has multiple issues:
1. OS-specific notes are missing for the `pycapnp` module.
2. `python3-zmq` is a package name in some Linux distros, rather than a Unix-wide convention.
3. Installing `pyzmq` from PyPI works in general, not only on macOS.

This PR resolves these issues. Additionally, two minor improvements have been added (see commit messages).
</description>

[2026-07-09] rc:3552217401 inline on test/README.md by hebasto (member) (edited 2026-07-09):
On OpenBSD, the situation is even [uglier](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/blob/443a32d692134943822172301636c15e77373d43/.github/workflows/openbsd.yml#L171-L186) than on NetBSD:
```yaml
          # The system's `capnproto` package ships static libraries
          # built without -fPIC, causing relocation errors when linking
          # pycapnp's shared extension module.
          #
          # A two-part workaround is applied:
          #  1. Force building the bundled libcapnp, which is compiled
          #     with -fPIC.
          #  2. Override LDCXXSHARED to drop the -L/usr/local/lib/ that
          #     Python's sysconfig injects ahead of the bundled library
          #     directories, and which would otherwise resolve -lcapnp*
          #     and -lkj* to the system's static archives.
          if pkg_info -e 'capnproto-*'; then
            LDCXXSHARED="c++ -pthread -shared -fPIC" pip3 install --break-system-packages pycapnp -C force-bundled-libcapnp=True
          else
            pip3 install --break-system-packages pycapnp
          fi
```

However, our current docs don't seem helpful for either NetBSD or OpenBSD users.
